items.item: Kafka Connect is a framework and runtime for implementing and operating source connectors that send records into Kafka and sink connectors that propagate records out
The Debezium server is a configurable, ready-to-use application that streams change events from a source database to a variety of messaging infrastructures
Change events can be sent to messaging infrastructures such as Amazon Kinesis, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, or Apache Pulsar
The Debezium engine runs not via Kafka Connect, but as a library embedded into a custom Java application

items.item: The event flattening SMT extracts the after field from a Debezium change event and replaces the original change event with only its after field
Instead of dropping the record that contains the before row data, the SMT can be configured to keep it
Configure the connector to use upsert mode so that data written to the sink database is idempotent, and replaying an event always produces the same final row state

items.item: The envelope-rebuild measurement uses one insert and one update from the same connection, decoded by the same slot, so the before-field contrast between them is the same stream's own two different outcomes, not two separately constructed records that might differ for unrelated reasons.

The unwrap measurement applies the identical hand-built transform function to both an update and a delete, confirming the delete's own __deleted-marker behavior is the same function's own branch, not a separately written special case.

The delete used for the unwrap measurement is captured under REPLICA IDENTITY FULL specifically so its before carries real column values rather than only a key, making the __deleted-plus-columns claim concrete rather than a __deleted-plus-nothing claim that a default-identity table would have produced.

The idempotent-upsert measurement applies the exact same record object twice rather than two separately constructed but equal records, ruling out any difference in construction as a confound and isolating the upsert statement itself as the only variable between the first write and the replay.

The row-count assertion after the replay (exactly one row) is checked in addition to the row's own final values, since a sink could in principle leave the visible values correct while still having silently inserted a second, duplicate row — the measurement rules out both failure modes, not just the more obvious one.

The wrong option in the first predict question — that column values alone are enough to distinguish a re-snapshot read from an insert — is ruled out by the measured unwrap function itself: nothing in its own output carries any trace of which op produced it, so the information needed to distinguish them is structurally gone, not merely hard to find.

The wrong option in the final predict question — that a sink stays consistent under replay regardless of insert mode — is ruled out directly by Debezium's own documentation, which ties idempotence specifically to upsert mode being configured, not to any property of the JDBC sink connector in general.

Every scratch table and replication slot this topic creates is confirmed dropped inside the same function that created it, verified by three successive clean runs of examples.py, and the shared orders table is never touched by any of this topic's four functions.
